title: Spin-polarized fusion fuel scale-up
bottleneck: Aligning the quantum spins of deuterium and tritium nuclei can increase fusion reaction rates, potentially cutting tritium consumption several-fold, but producing, transporting, and injecting spin-polarized fuel without depolarization is unsolved. Polarized pellets depolarize on contact with walls and magnetic field gradients, and no polarized fueling system has operated on a tokamak. The physics is attractive; the engineering is nearly untouched. Depolarization happens in milliseconds on contact with most surfaces, so the entire fueling path from production to plasma must be redesigned around spin preservation.
why_it_blocks: Spin polarization could relax the tritium breeding requirement that gates the whole D-T economy, but only if the fuel survives the journey from production to plasma core.
current_state: Modeling suggests large reductions in tritium needs with polarization. Experimental polarized-fuel injection into fusion plasmas has not been demonstrated.
